sections.agent_rules:
1. Never ask the user for an API key, token or password, and never accept one pasted into the chat.
2. Never read, print, grep or open `.env`, `.dev.vars` or any file holding a credential; never put a key in code, logs, commits or command arguments.
3. Check what is available first: `authinjector status`.
4. Make every call through the broker: `authinjector call <service> <METHOD> <path> [--data ...]` (or curl over the socket). The broker adds the key; the response comes back unchanged.
5. On an error, tell the user the exact command from the troubleshooting list instead of asking for a key.
6. More help: `authinjector help`, `authinjector help <service>`, the help MCP at https://authinjector.com/mcp, and https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector.
sections.clients:
Help-only MCP server (no keys, no API calls, no user data): Streamable HTTP at https://authinjector.com/mcp.

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http authinjector-help https://authinjector.com/mcp`
- Claude.ai / Claude Desktop: Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector, URL `https://authinjector.com/mcp`
- Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers":{"authinjector-help":{"url":"https://authinjector.com/mcp"}}}`

Agent instructions, generated from the catalogue:

- Claude skill: copy `skills/authinjector/` into `~/.claude/skills/` (or a project's `.claude/skills/`) — https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector/blob/main/skills/authinjector/SKILL.md
- Cursor rule: copy `.cursor/rules/authinjector.mdc` into your project — https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector/blob/main/.cursor/rules/authinjector.mdc
- Codex, Cursor and others: add the AuthInjector section of AGENTS.md — https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- GitHub Copilot: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector/blob/main/.github/copilot-instructions.md
sections.install:
Install the latest release (Linux, x86_64 or arm64):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://authinjector.com/dl/$(uname -m) | tar xz
cd authinjector-$(uname -m)-unknown-linux-musl
sudo ./install.sh --caller "$USER"
```

Each release lists `SHA256SUMS.txt` (https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector/releases/latest); verify with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`.

Build from source (static musl, needs Docker for `cross`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/blacksq-com/authinjector && cd authinjector
cargo install cross
cross build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
sudo ./install.sh --caller "$USER"
```
sections.overview:
AuthInjector is a local broker that holds API keys so AI agents and scripts never do. A caller sends plain HTTP to a Unix socket with no credential; the broker reads the caller's identity from the kernel (SO_PEERCRED), checks that caller's allowlist and rate limit for that key, injects the key, forwards the call and returns the upstream response unchanged. One audit line per call.

Platform: Linux only (SO_PEERCRED). Windows: run in WSL2. macOS: not supported yet.
sections.setup:
Keys are added by the user, never by an agent, and never as an argument:

```bash
sudo authinjector add <service> -c <user> -r 20      # prompts for the key, echo off
sudo authinjector add <service> -c <user> -l work    # a second key for the same service
sudo systemctl restart authinjector
authinjector status                                 # what this user may call
authinjector help <service>                         # how to call one service
```

Update the service catalogue from the repo with `sudo authinjector catalogue update` (shows a diff; a change that would send a configured key to a new host or slot must be confirmed at a terminal).
sections.troubleshooting:
- `no broker socket` / `connection refused`: the broker is not running, or the user is not in `authinjector-clients`. Tell the user: `systemctl status authinjector.socket`; `sudo usermod -aG authinjector-clients "$USER"` then log out and back in (or `sg authinjector-clients -c '...'`).
- 403: the caller is not allowlisted for that key, method or path. Tell the user: `sudo authinjector add <service> -c <your-user>` (or add you to that key's callers / widen its endpoints in /etc/authinjector/config.toml), then `sudo systemctl restart authinjector`.
- 404: unknown service or label. `authinjector status` lists what this caller may use; labelled keys are `<service>:<label>`.
- 405: method not allowed on that path; `authinjector help <service>` lists the allowed ones.
- 429: rate limited per caller and key. Wait, do not retry in a loop.
- 502: the upstream could not be reached.

services.help:
### Clio (`clio`)

- Base URL: https://app.clio.com
- Key injected as: header Authorization: Bearer <key>
- Get a key: https://app.clio.com/settings/developer_applications
- Allowed:
  - GET, POST /api/v4

Call it (the broker adds the key):

```bash
authinjector call clio GET /api/v4
curl --unix-socket /run/authinjector/authinjector.sock 'http://localhost/clio/api/v4'
```

A second key for the same service is addressed as `clio:<label>`, e.g. `authinjector call clio:work ...`.
services.name: Clio
